ConocoPhillips rose slightly today, but the stock has fallen sharply over the past two weeks—down 8.65% since early November—as oil prices have collapsed. Brent crude dropped below $90 a barrel yesterday for the first time since August on hopes that the Iran conflict is de-escalating, with President Trump signaling the war could end soon. For an oil producer like ConocoPhillips, lower crude prices directly squeeze profit margins, which is why the stock has been under pressure despite today's modest bounce.

The broader headwind is geopolitical: earlier in the period, Iran tensions had supported higher oil prices, but a shift toward peace talk has reversed that support. US oil is now trading at $99.64 per barrel versus $107 globally, indicating weakness in the domestic market. Until crude prices stabilize or geopolitical risk rises again, large integrated oil producers face continued downside.
